title: Suppressing Two Signals of Aging: Insights from the 2025 Rapamycin–Trametinib Study | Healthspan
abstract: **Dual Pathway Targeting as a Systems-Level Strategy.** The 2025 *Nature Aging* study showed that combining rapamycin and trametinib extended lifespan by 34.9% in females and 27.4% in males—significantly exceeding either drug alone. That question took center stage in 2025, when a groundbreaking study published in *Nature Aging* by Gkioni and colleagues tested a bold hypothesis: that combining rapamycin with trametinib, a cancer drug that blocks another major growth signal, might more effectively slow aging. [5] Each of these compounds targets a distinct arm of cellular signaling: rapamycin inhibits mTORC1, trametinib blocks MEK in the Ras–MEK–ERK pathway, and lithium inhibits glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3), a key enzyme in metabolism and cellular regulation. A 2025 study published in *Nature Aging,* titled "*The geroprotectors trametinib and rapamycin combine additively to extend mouse healthspan and lifespan*" by Gkioni et al., took this next step by examining the effects of these two compounds, both individually and in combination, in mice.
